title: Aperture: A Patch-Aware Framework for Joint Forgery Detection and Localization
decisive_datasets_tasks: Training/localization use the DDL collection of roughly 1.5 million single-face and multi-face tampering images across 61 facial-manipulation techniques; detection tests use face-deepfake benchmarks such as FaceForensics++, Celeb-DF, and DeeperForensics.
mechanism: Patch-aware local/global classification plus query-guided segmentation and pseudo-label test-time adaptation.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: None. The dataset construction and external benchmarks are facial manipulation/deepfake data.
rationale: Joint detection/localization does not broaden the corpus scope when every decisive benchmark is facial forgery.

title: Revisiting Deepfake Detection: BCNet for Robust Generalization Beyond Semantic Dependence
decisive_datasets_tasks: The official implementation trains/tests AI-generated still-image detection across non-face content categories and unseen generators, with examples including car/cat imagery and test generators such as DALL-E 3, FLUX.1-dev, Stable Diffusion, and StyleGAN3.
mechanism: A general AI-generated-image detector designed to reduce reliance on semantic content and retain generator-artifact cues.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: Yes. Non-face, general-content still images from multiple GAN and text-to-image families are separate evaluated conditions.
rationale: The paper's use of the word deepfake is broader than facial deepfakes; its actual experiments directly cover general synthetic still images.

title: Pixels Don't Lie (but Your Detector Might): Bootstrapping MLLM-as-a-Judge for Trustworthy Deepfake Detection and Reasoning Supervision
decisive_datasets_tasks: DeepfakeJudge-Detect contains 2,000 still images: 1,000 OpenImages-V7 real images, 500 text-to-image fakes from Gemini/SeedDream, and 500 generatively edited images from Gemini, FLUX Kontext Max, and Qwen-Edit. DeepfakeJudge-Reason separately evaluates detection/reasoning and localization-grounded explanations.
mechanism: An MLLM judge bootstrapped with generator-evaluator feedback scores the fidelity of deepfake decisions and natural-language visual reasoning.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: Yes. Fully generated and generatively edited general OpenImages-style still content are substantive benchmark partitions.
rationale: The contribution directly evaluates broad AIGI and generative editing rather than only faces or video.

title: Fake-GPT: Detecting Fake Image via Large Language Model
decisive_datasets_tasks: The reported generalization protocol trains on ProGAN imagery and tests GAN families including StyleGAN, StyleGAN2, BigGAN, CycleGAN, StarGAN, GauGAN, and DeepFake, with real-image sources spanning LSUN, ImageNet, CelebA/CelebA-HQ, and COCO; diffusion-generated sets are also evaluated.
mechanism: RGB pixels are serialized as token sequences and a Qwen-7B model is adapted with LoRA for real/fake image classification.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: Yes. LSUN/ImageNet/COCO content and BigGAN/CycleGAN/GauGAN/diffusion tests extend beyond facial imagery.
rationale: The generator and source-domain experiments constitute broad still-image AIGI detection even though the paper uses 'deepfake' terminology.

title: A Swin Transformer and CLIP-Based Framework for Generalized DeepFake Detection
decisive_datasets_tasks: A publisher-accessible primary experiments section was not available. Index snippets report nine unseen GAN models and an Ojha diffusion-image benchmark, but the exact image domains and table definitions could not be verified from the primary paper.
mechanism: Swin Transformer and CLIP feature fusion for cross-generator fake-image classification.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: Plausible but not primary-verified; the indexed summary suggests GAN and diffusion still-image experiments that may include general imagery.
exact_evidence_needed: Inspect the primary experimental dataset table and sample descriptions: do the nine GAN tests and the Ojha diffusion benchmark contain independently scored non-face general still images, and what metrics are reported for them?
rationale: Thin publisher metadata cannot safely distinguish a broad AIGI detector from a face-only detector; removal would risk a false exclusion.

title: On Attribution of Deepfakes
decisive_datasets_tasks: The attribution experiment uses 6,000 centered 1024x1024 human-face images, 2,000 each from ProgressiveGAN, StyleGAN, and StyleGAN2, and performs seed/source reconstruction and attribution.
mechanism: GAN inversion/reconstruction is used to attribute a generated face to its source model and latent seed.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: None. The primary paper explicitly describes all evaluated samples as human faces.
rationale: Source attribution is in scope as a task only when it extends beyond a face-only benchmark; this paper does not.

title: Dual-Tree Complex Wavelet Driven Hierarchical Spatial-Frequency Fusion Learning for Robust Deepfake Detection
decisive_datasets_tasks: The primary abstract discloses cross-dataset AUROC on Celeb-DFv2 and DFDC, both facial-video deepfake benchmarks, but refers generically to additional benchmark datasets without naming their domains.
mechanism: Hierarchical spatial-frequency fusion and dual-tree complex-wavelet directional subband modeling for deepfake classification.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: Not established. The named evaluations are face/video only, while the complete dataset list is unavailable.
exact_evidence_needed: Do the full primary dataset and results tables contain any independently scored benchmark with non-face fully generated or generatively edited still images, and what are all train/test benchmarks?
rationale: The named evidence points to face/video drift, but the abstract is insufficient to rule out a substantive broader experiment.

title: Beyond the Spectrum: Detecting Deepfakes via Re-Synthesis
decisive_datasets_tasks: Detection experiments cover real CelebA-HQ, FFHQ, and LSUN imagery and generated outputs from ProGAN, StyleGAN, StyleGAN2, StarGAN2, with re-synthesis networks trained on both face and LSUN scene domains.
mechanism: Images are re-synthesized by super-resolution, denoising, or colorization networks; discrepancies and residual artifacts drive real/fake classification.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: Yes. LSUN scene imagery supplies an independently evaluated non-face domain in addition to face datasets.
rationale: The evaluated task is general GAN-generated still-image detection across face and scene domains.

title: Comparative Analysis of Custom CNN Architecture and MobileNet for Deepfake Image Detection
decisive_datasets_tasks: The primary abstract reports binary detection on CIFAKE: 120,000 images split evenly between CIFAR-10 real images and Stable-Diffusion-generated synthetic counterparts, with custom CNN and MobileNetV2 comparisons.
mechanism: Custom CNN and transfer-learned MobileNetV2 classifiers distinguish real from AI-generated still images.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: Yes. CIFAKE contains diverse CIFAR-10 object/scene classes rather than a face-only corpus.
rationale: This is directly a broad synthetic still-image detection experiment despite its deepfake label.

title: Universal Deepfake Detection via Low-Rank Adaptation of Vision-Language Models
decisive_datasets_tasks: The primary abstract reports mAP/accuracy, robustness, and scale ablations but does not name the training or evaluation datasets, generator families, or image domains.
mechanism: LoRA is inserted into both visual and text encoders of a vision-language model and optimized with contrastive loss.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: Not established from accessible primary material.
exact_evidence_needed: Does the primary experimental dataset table and generator list show that the reported mAP includes independently evaluated non-face general AIGI rather than only facial deepfakes?
rationale: The word 'universal' and broad references do not establish experimental scope without named primary datasets.

title: Diffusion Models as a Representation Learner for Deepfake Image Detection
decisive_datasets_tasks: The primary proceedings experiment reports classification on FaceForensics++ using DDIM reconstructions, latent inversion, and high-frequency features.
mechanism: A diffusion model is used as a representation/reconstruction learner to expose artifacts for downstream deepfake classification.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: None. Diffusion is the analysis mechanism; diffusion-generated general images are not a separate detection benchmark.
rationale: Using a diffusion model internally does not broaden a face-manipulation-only evaluation into synthetic-image detection.

title: Enhancing Sensing and Imaging Capabilities Through Surface Plasmon Resonance for Deepfake Image Detection
decisive_datasets_tasks: The primary abstract reports greater than 95% accuracy from a gold-nanoparticle SPR spectroscopic setup but does not identify the images, dataset, generation/manipulation methods, sample counts, or train/test protocol.
mechanism: A physical surface-plasmon-resonance sensing setup is claimed to detect minute alterations in image content through spectral shifts.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: Not established; the primary preview gives no auditable image-domain or generator evidence.
exact_evidence_needed: Inspect the full primary methods, dataset/sample table, and results: what exact authentic and fake images were physically measured, were any non-face AIGI or generative edits independently evaluated, and how were splits and labels defined?
rationale: A reported accuracy without identifiable data cannot support either retention or confident exclusion.

title: Breaking Manifold Continuity: Vector Quantized Modeling for Real-Centric Deepfake Detection
decisive_datasets_tasks: The accessible primary abstract states only that experiments use 'diverse datasets'; the OpenReview primary PDF was unavailable for inspection, so dataset names, domains, and generator-level results remain unverified.
mechanism: A CLIP vision encoder is constrained with a vector-quantized real-image codebook and adaptive tangent-space projection for open-set fake detection.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: Plausible but not primary-verified.
exact_evidence_needed: Which training/testing datasets and image categories appear in the primary experiments table, and are there separate quantitative results on non-face general GAN/diffusion still images?
rationale: The method language is compatible with broad AIGI detection, but the abstract alone cannot establish the decisive experimental scope.

title: An Improved Dense CNN Architecture for Deepfake Image Detection
decisive_datasets_tasks: The full paper uses real CelebA/FFHQ faces and fake faces from GDWCT, AttGAN, StarGAN, StyleGAN, and StyleGAN2; external testing extracts/crops faces from Celeb-DF video.
mechanism: A densely connected CNN performs real/fake classification on aligned facial images.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: None. Every real and synthetic source in the experimental section is facial.
rationale: Multiple generators do not make the evaluation broad when all generated content is faces.

title: SpectraGuard: Provably-Private Deepfake Detection with Learnable Frequency-Domain Differential Privacy
decisive_datasets_tasks: Detection/privacy experiments use FaceForensics++ and Celeb-DF, including reconstruction attacks against protected facial inputs.
mechanism: DEConv preprocessing and block-DCT differential privacy suppress identity-revealing facial information while retaining forgery cues.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: None. Both decisive benchmarks and the privacy threat model are explicitly face-based.
rationale: This is privacy-preserving face-deepfake detection, with no broader still-image AIGI evaluation.

title: ODDN: Addressing Unpaired Data Challenges in Open-World Deepfake Detection on Online Social Networks
decisive_datasets_tasks: The primary experiments train on ForenSynths object categories and evaluate 17 generated-image datasets/families, including InfoGAN, BEGAN, CramerGAN, MMDGAN, RelGAN, S3GAN, SNGAN, STGGAN, ProGAN, StyleGAN/2, BigGAN, CycleGAN, StarGAN, GauGAN, and DeepFake under social-network compression.
mechanism: Open-world data aggregation learns from paired/unpaired raw and compressed images; compression-discard gradient correction reduces sensitivity to OSN processing.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: Yes. Chair, horse, car, cat, and other general object categories are quantitatively evaluated across many GAN families.
rationale: The paper is a broad synthetic still-image detector despite calling the task open-world deepfake detection.

title: Comparative Analysis of Deepfake Image Detection Method Using VGG16, VGG19 and ResNet50
decisive_datasets_tasks: The study classifies 1,200 images, split between 600 real images and 600 FaceApp-manipulated face images, using VGG16, VGG19, and ResNet50.
mechanism: Transfer-learned CNN classifiers detect FaceApp facial manipulation.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: None. The sole fake source is a face-editing application and the samples are faces.
rationale: This is a small face-manipulation classifier without a broader generative-image test.

title: Deepfake Image Detection Using ResNet50 Model
decisive_datasets_tasks: The primary abstract names DeepFakeFace and Deepfake Processed, with 4,000 images per dataset and ResNet50/Gaussian-blur experiments, but does not disclose the underlying image domains or manipulation/generator composition.
mechanism: Gaussian-blur preprocessing with ResNet50 binary classification.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: Not established from the accessible primary abstract; the dataset names suggest face imagery but are not sufficient proof of exclusive scope.
exact_evidence_needed: Inspect the primary dataset section and sample figures for both DeepFakeFace and Deepfake Processed: are all images faces, and is any non-face fully generated or generatively edited still-image subset reported separately?
rationale: A face-only interpretation is likely, but the primary abstract does not establish dataset composition strongly enough for irreversible classification.

title: Enhancing Deepfake Detection with Diversified Self-Blending Images and Residuals
decisive_datasets_tasks: Training uses diversified self-blended facial images; cross-dataset tests train on FaceForensics++ and evaluate FaceForensics++ HQ/LQ, Celeb-DF, and WildDeepfake.
mechanism: Facial color/frequency conversion, mask deformation, self-blending, and residual supervision expose face-forgery artifacts.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: None. All completed experiments are facial manipulation/deepfake benchmarks.
rationale: Synthetic self-blending is training augmentation for face-deepfake detection, not broader synthetic-image evaluation.

title: Deepfake Image Detection Using Light-Weight Attention Integrated MobileNetV3 Model
decisive_datasets_tasks: The publisher abstract compares MobileNetV3 with XceptionNet, InceptionV3, EfficientNetB0, and InceptionResNet and reports an F-score of 98.46%, but names no dataset or image domain.
mechanism: Self-attention-enhanced MobileNetV3 for lightweight real-time fake-image classification.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: Not established from accessible primary evidence.
exact_evidence_needed: What dataset and manipulation/generator sources appear in the full primary results, are the samples all faces, and does any non-face AIGI subset have a separate result?
rationale: Architecture and score alone do not determine whether the contribution is face-only or broad synthetic-image detection.

title: The Face Deepfake Detection Challenge
decisive_datasets_tasks: Challenge tasks are face-deepfake detection and source-face reconstruction. Real data come from CelebA and FFHQ; fake faces come from StarGAN, StarGAN-v2, StyleGAN, StyleGAN2, AttGAN, and GDWCT, with additional face crops from DFDC/FaceForensics++ in participant development.
mechanism: Challenge benchmark and comparative evaluation of face classification/reconstruction systems, primarily EfficientNet-family detectors.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: None. The challenge is explicitly restricted to face images and facial generators/manipulations.
rationale: The paper's entire contribution is a face-deepfake benchmark.

title: Deep Learning for Deepfakes Creation and Detection: A Survey
decisive_datasets_tasks: The survey organizes image and video deepfake creation/detection around face synthesis, identity replacement, reenactment, facial attributes/artifacts, and face/video benchmarks such as FaceForensics++, Celeb-DF, DFDC, UADFV, and DeepfakeTIMIT.
mechanism: Survey/taxonomy of deepfake creation and detection methods, divided mainly into image-frame and temporal/video approaches.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: No substantive broader still-image AIGI review contribution is separated from the face/deepfake literature.
rationale: Although surveys may remain when they cover the corpus scope, this review surveys facial deepfakes and video rather than general synthetic still-image detection/attribution.

title: Complement Face Forensic Detection and Localization with FacialLandmarks
decisive_datasets_tasks: The proposed 1.3-million-image dataset uses CelebA/FFHQ real faces, DCGAN/LSGAN/BEGAN/WGAN-GP/ProGAN/StyleGAN generated faces, and StarGAN/SEFCGAN edited faces; external tests use FaceForensics++.
mechanism: An Xception-based dual classification/localization network incorporates facial-landmark maps and pixel masks.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: None. Fully generated and edited samples are explicitly all facial images.
rationale: Generative editing and full synthesis are present, but only in a face-restricted benchmark, which the narrowed policy treats as drift.

title: Beyond Backbones: Degradation-Aware Prototype Fusion for Robust Deepfake Detection
decisive_datasets_tasks: The method is trained/evaluated on the NTIRE 2026 Robust Deepfake Detection face-forgery benchmark, with 26 image degradations and AUC as the principal metric.
mechanism: Degradation-conditioned fusion of LoRA-adapted CLIP and DINOv3 branches with generator-aware prototypes and anomaly-aware local pooling.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: None. The challenge paper explicitly frames and evaluates generative face synthesis/face forgery.
rationale: Robustness to degradations does not broaden the underlying face-forgery task.

title: Lightweight Image Forgery Detection via Tucker Decomposition for Efficient Edge Deployment
decisive_datasets_tasks: The primary abstract says three detectors are compressed and tested across 24 forgery datasets, but it does not name those datasets, their content domains, or the per-dataset results.
mechanism: Unified Tucker decomposition compresses image-, frequency-, and pretrained-model-based forgery detectors for edge deployment.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: Not established from accessible primary material; the count of 24 datasets alone does not distinguish general AIGI from collections of face-deepfake benchmarks.
exact_evidence_needed: What are all 24 datasets and three base detectors in the primary tables, and do they include separate quantitative results on non-face GAN/diffusion/general synthetic still imagery?
rationale: The breadth claim is promising but too underspecified to support either retention or exclusion.

title: Artifact-Aware Explainable Deepfake Detection via Fake-Only High-Frequency Alignment Supervision
decisive_datasets_tasks: The primary abstract reports EfficientNet-B0 detection, Grad-CAM/FFT alignment, a 0.262 alignment gap, and 99.96% validation accuracy, but gives no dataset name or image composition; diverse cross-domain and video tests are only future work.
mechanism: Fake-only high-frequency alignment loss encourages CNN attention maps to overlap FFT-derived forensic artifact regions.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: Not established; no completed broad dataset is named.
exact_evidence_needed: What is the validation corpus in the primary dataset/method section, is it face-only, which generator/edit types are included, and was any non-face general AIGI subset actually evaluated rather than proposed as future work?
rationale: The current primary evidence supports a detector result but does not reveal the content scope.

title: HiDD-Net: A Hierarchical Dual-Domain Distillation Network for Efficient Deepfake Detection
decisive_datasets_tasks: No primary abstract, experimental table, or accessible paper text identifies the datasets or image domains.
mechanism: Title-level evidence suggests hierarchical spatial/frequency distillation for an efficient deepfake detector, but the primary implementation details could not be audited.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: Unknown.
exact_evidence_needed: What train/test datasets, generator/manipulation types, and media types are in the SPIE primary paper, and are separate results reported for any non-face generated or edited still-image benchmark?
rationale: There is insufficient primary experimental evidence for any reliable scope decision.

title: LADLE-MM: Limited Annotation Based Detector with Learned Ensembles for Multimodal Misinformation
decisive_datasets_tasks: DGM4 binary/multi-label experiments classify pristine/tampered image-text pairs with visual labels Face Swap and Face Attribute plus Text Swap and Text Attribute; VERITE tests open-set multimodal misinformation/out-of-context consistency rather than synthetic-image authenticity.
mechanism: ViT, DeBERTa, and frozen BLIP branches are fused with learned model-soup initialization for multimodal misinformation classification.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: None. DGM4's synthetic visual operations are face-only, while VERITE's broader images are evaluated for image-text misinformation, not synthetic-image detection or attribution.
rationale: The paper is valuable multimodal misinformation work, but its synthetic-image component is face manipulation only and its broader task is outside this corpus.

title: Omni-Fake: Benchmarking Unified Multimodal Social Media Deepfake Detection
decisive_datasets_tasks: The image modality alone contains hundreds of thousands of real, fully synthetic, and tampered still images in Omni-Fake-Set plus a held-out Omni-Fake-OOD image benchmark; detection, localization, explanation, and OOD generalization are quantitatively evaluated.
mechanism: A unified multimodal dataset and reinforcement-learning-driven detector produce authenticity labels, localization, and explanations across image, audio, video, and talking-head modalities.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: Yes. The image split includes broad scene/object content with fully synthetic and partial-edit labels, independently evaluated from the audio/video modalities.
rationale: A multimodal paper remains in scope because it contains a large, substantive, independently evaluated broad still-image AIGI contribution.

title: Deepfake detection using deep learning methods: A systematic and comprehensive review
decisive_datasets_tasks: The systematic review categorizes deepfake detection into image, video, audio, and hybrid media, with its visual evidence centered on facial synthesis/manipulation, face replacement/reenactment, and established face/video deepfake datasets; it reports that video dominates the included literature.
mechanism: Systematic literature review and taxonomy of deep-learning deepfake detectors.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: No separately developed review contribution on general non-face synthetic still-image detection or attribution is established.
rationale: Survey status does not override scope: this review treats facial and audiovisual deepfakes rather than the broader synthetic still-image field.

title: Detecting fake images by identifying potential texture difference
decisive_datasets_tasks: The primary paper defines Deepfake as face manipulation/replacement and evaluates ResNet18 classification after saliency-guided texture enhancement on real and fake face images.
mechanism: Image saliency and guided filtering amplify facial texture differences before ResNet18 real/fake classification.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: None. The methods, contributions, and experiments repeatedly specify face texture and fake face images.
rationale: This is a face-texture deepfake detector without an independent general-image benchmark.

title: Detection of real-time deep fakes and face forgery in video conferencing employing generative adversarial networks
decisive_datasets_tasks: The full open primary article trains on CelebA-HQ faces and FaceForensics++ video frames for real-time video-conferencing face-forgery detection.
mechanism: A compact ensemble of discriminators with a deep conditional GAN operates on frames extracted from video-conference streams.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: None. CelebA-HQ and FaceForensics++ are facial, and the operational task is video conferencing.
rationale: Frame extraction from video does not create a broad still-image contribution when all evaluated content is faces.

title: A Guided-Based Approach for Deepfake Detection: RGB-Depth Integration via Features Fusion
decisive_datasets_tasks: The full primary paper crops subject faces and evaluates on FaceForensics++ videos covering DeepFakes, Face2Face, FaceSwap, and NeuralTextures facial manipulations, including adversarial-robustness tests.
mechanism: Separate MobileNetV2 RGB and monocular-depth branches are fused with RGB-guided attention for face-deepfake classification.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: None. The sole benchmark and all manipulation classes are facial.
rationale: The depth cue is evaluated only for face manipulations extracted from video.
